newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Petkim workers stage wage protest.
newsitem.headline: Turk Petkim workers stage wage protest.

text.p: Around 3,500 workers at Turkey's largely state-owned petrochemicals producer Petrokimya Holding A.S. (Petkim) launched a protest for higher wages, a union official said on Tuesday.
The workers, members of the Petrol-Is union, held a sit-in and stopped goods dispatches at Petkim's Aliaga plant near the western port city of Izmir.

Local Petrol-Is representative Mustafa Oztaskin said in a statement that the employer had not obeyed an article in the labour contract calling for wages of new employees to be raised in tandem with the rise in the minimum wage.

But Petkim General Manager Mehmet Yilmaz said he supported the union demands and was talking to the government about them. "I believe their demands will be met and this will lead to a fairer pay system and a peaceful working environment," he said in a statement.
The Turkish government had raised the minimum wage by 101 percent year-on-year on August 1.
The government holds 95.86 percent of Petkim, which is slated for privatisation.
